extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and processing affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 and applying AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 exceptions (including joint research agreements), plus handling improper inventorship during patent examination and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 — prima facie showing required
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) or (b) must show that either (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or (2) the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure or before effective filing, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affida vit/declaration need not show the prior disclosure was 'enabling' under 35 U.S.C. 112(a); it must establish the fact of the inventor-origin or prior public disclosure (see § 2155.04 enabling discussion). If the declaration shows the inventor made the earlier public disclosure that predates an intervening reference, the examiner should withdraw an anticipation rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1). For printed-publication prior disclosures, 37 CFR 1.130(b)(1) requires a copy of the printed publication be included with the declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting evidence for inventor-origin disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation accompanying a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit/declaration should provide evidence that the subject matter originated with the inventor or joint inventor and that the subject matter was communicated (directly or indirectly) to the entity that later made the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: presentation slides from a conference, copies of communications to an assignee or collaborator, or an inventor's oath/declaration already of record. The record should contain sufficient evidence to establish the inventor as the source of the disclosed subject matter; the MPEP examples illustrate withdrawing an anticipation when copies (e.g., slides) and inventor declarations are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include copies of printed prior disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior public disclosure relied upon is a printed publication, 37 CFR 1.130(b)(1) requires that a copy of that printed publication be included with the declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supply required copies may prevent the affidavit/declaration from serving as the required evidence to overcome a rejection based on that printed publication. The MPEP examples show supplying a copy of conference presentation slides when asserting a prior public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or patent owner may submit an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130. When an assignee, obligated assignee, or person showing sufficient proprietary interest is the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 118 rather than the inventor, the applicant (or their representative) must be the party that files the affidavit or declaration even if the inventor signed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration must be filed by a party having authority to take action in the application; authority to file generally does not lie with the inventor if the inventor is not the applicant. See MPEP § 717.01(c) for authority details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.130 is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.130 are not available if the rejection is based on a disclosure made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention (i.e., beyond the statutory grace), or in situations where applying 1.130 would result in issuing or confirming two patents containing patentably indistinct claims to different parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also not available if the rejection is based upon a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication naming another inventor that claims the same or substantially the same invention and the affidavit/declaration contends derivation — because that could lead to two patents to different inventive entities (see In re Deckler). In those cases, petitioning for a derivation proceeding (37 CFR 42.401 et seq.) may be appropriate (37 CFR 1.130(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement is not required for 1.130 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) or (b) need not demonstrate that the inventor's or other's prior disclosure was an 'enabling' disclosure within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1.130 submission must only show the factual predicates in (1) or (2) (i.e., who made or obtained the disclosure and the timing) rather than technical enablement. Note, however, that enablement still matters for anticipation under 102, but 1.130 is about establishment of prior public disclosure origin/timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement exception under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: To treat subject matter disclosed by another as commonly owned (and thus not available as prior art under 102(a)(2)), three conditions must be met: (1) the subject matter disclosed was developed and the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of one or more parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the effective filing date; (2) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (3) the application for patent discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'joint research agreement' is defined as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement between two or more persons or entities for experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention (35 U.S.C. 100(h)). To invoke the exception, applicant must provide a signed statement asserting the facts (on or beginning on a separate sheet and signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b)), amend the application to include the parties' names (37 CFR 1.71(g)), and pay any required processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) unless the amendment is timely per 1.17(g)(2). The Office will not request corroborating evidence absent independent evidence raising doubt about the agreement's existence or nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and content requirements for invoking common-ownership or JRA exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke common-owner/JRA exceptions (e.g., 102(b)(2)(C) or 102(c)), the applicant must present a conspicuous statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person no later than the effective filing date, or that the JRA conditions were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should be on or begin on a separate sheet and must not be directed to other matters (37 CFR 1.4(c)), and must be signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b). If names of parties to the JRA are not in the application, amend to add them and include any required processing fee. Failure to provide the required statement will result in a 102/103 rejection using the reference (see form paragraph 7.20.04.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of common ownership for joint inventors and applicant duties
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application names joint inventors, the examiner presumes that the subject matter of claims was commonly owned at the time inventions were effectively filed absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised (and obligated under 37 CFR 1.56) to point out the inventor and effective filing dates of any claim that was not commonly owned at the time a later invention was effectively filed so the examiner can consider 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). Use this paragraph in all applications with joint inventors unless claims clearly limit to a single invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper inventorship — statutory and procedural consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent laws require naming the inventor(s) for any invention claimed in the application (35 U.S.C. 115). If an application names a person who is not an actual inventor or joint inventor, it should be handled via derivation proceedings (35 U.S.C. 135), correction of inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48, or by rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorrect inventorship is evident and no request to correct under 37 CFR 1.48 has been filed, the examiner should reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115. MPEP provides form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.04.101.aia, 7.04.102.aia, 7.04.02.aia) and notes on how to state the basis for improper inventorship rejections and follow-on paragraphs to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 — timing and application of obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 103, obviousness is determined as of the effective filing date of the claimed invention (rather than as of the date the claimed invention was made). AIA 103 requires consideration of 'the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, pre-AIA obviousness practice largely continues to apply, but examiners must use the effective filing date as the relevant date. Non-enabling disclosures are still prior art 'for all they teach' for purposes of obviousness under 103. Examiners should follow MPEP § 2141 et seq. and USPTO patent examination guidance when formulating obviousness rationales. Use specified form paragraphs (e.g., 7.20.aia and related paragraphs) where required (first actions on the merits and final rejections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and Office action usage rules for AIA 102/103 citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs are prescribed for Office actions involving AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections (e.g., ¶ 7.06, ¶ 7.20.aia, ¶ 7.20.01.aia, ¶ 7.20.02.aia, ¶ 7.20.04.aia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes when to use statutory text (e.g., 7.20.aia only in first actions on the merits employing 35 U.S.C. 103 and final rejections), that certain paragraphs must precede others (e.g., 7.03.aia must precede 7.20.aia), and that some paragraphs should be used only once per Office action. Form paragraphs also instruct examiners on content to include (identify references, common assignees, explain failures to provide required statements, etc.).
